worksheet.deviation: No flow through SDV-101 on a spurious HIPPS trip
worksheet.cause: Single PT drift or a plugged impulse tapping trips the 1oo2 loop (no 2oo3 voting); logic-solver fault or a partial-stroke test left in the tripped state.
worksheet.consequence: Instant loss of 137.1 MMscfd sales gas and 2,936 bbl/d condensate; wells keep flowing at up to 95 bara against a closed SDV-101 and restart needs full HIPPS reset and HP repressurisation.
worksheet.safeguard: HIPPS 1oo2 PT / SIL-3 logic solver, 12-month proof test and partial-stroke test; SDV-101 <2 s closure; upstream choke and ESD.
worksheet.action: Add 2oo3 voting or a trip filter/delay to reject single-PT transients, separate the two impulse lines and write the HIPPS trip/restart procedure; trend nuisance trips (HAZ-02).

worksheet.deviation: SDV-101 does not close on a HIPPS demand
worksheet.cause: Sand/condensate erosion of the 316L/Duplex trim or seat, actuator spring/solenoid failure or loss of instrument air; proof test is partial-stroke only and the final element is single.
worksheet.consequence: V-101 and the 66 barg inlet are exposed to 95 bara wellhead pressure (72.6 bara MIP exceeded); PSV-101 alone must pass 42.63 kg/s (91.1% of flare now, 107.5% after +18%); loss of containment with jet-fire potential.
worksheet.safeguard: PSV-101 P orifice 6.38 in2 (5.53 in2 required at +18%, 86.7%) set 66 barg; HIPPS 1oo2 PT, SIL-3 logic, <2 s closure; SDV-101 100 barg ANSI 900 body.
worksheet.action: Device-specific SIL verification and full-stroke proof test; add a redundant actuator/solenoid or diverse final element and confirm trim material against sand erosion (HAZ-02).

worksheet.deviation: HP inlet pressure above the 66 barg design (wellhead up to 95 bara)
worksheet.cause: Well control or choke failure, or a surging well near the 95 bara shut-in; the HIPPS trip setpoint is not stated, so the trip-to-PSV margin is undefined; a blocked tapping reads low and delays the trip.
worksheet.consequence: Inlet line and pipeline to 72.6 bara MIP, V-101 at 110% of design with only 3 mm CA on a ten-year-old shell; a late trip lifts PSV-101 into a flare already at 91.1% (107.5% after the re-rate).
worksheet.safeguard: HIPPS SIL-3 loop with 1oo2 PT and SDV-101; PSV-101 6.38 in2 at 66 barg; upstream wellhead choke.
worksheet.action: Define the HIPPS trip setpoint, deadband and response time with a LOPA, confirm PT taps are downstream of SDV-101, and verify the 72.6 bara MIP case in the relief study (HAZ-02, HAZ-01).

worksheet.deviation: Wellstream above 363 K (90 C) at SDV-101 and V-101
worksheet.cause: Hot well or reduced Joule-Thomson cooling as the choke is opened for rate; a workover returning hotter fluid.
worksheet.consequence: Only 10 K margin to the 100 C design of SDV-101/V-101; 316L seals and gaskets approach their limit and the CO2 inhibition basis (0.15 mm/yr at 81 C) is no longer qualified.
worksheet.safeguard: 100 C design temperature on V-101 and SDV-101; PIR 50 mm insulation; continuous CO2 inhibition.
worksheet.action: Add a high-temperature alarm on the HP inlet, qualify the inhibitor and 316L seals to 100 C, and set a choke/rate limit for hot-well operation (HAZ-06).

worksheet.deviation: Only one of the two HIPPS pressure transmitters is in service
worksheet.cause: Both PTs on a common impulse tapping/root valve so one plugging event disables both; one PT isolated for calibration without a compensating trip; DC 0.6 leaves 40% of dangerous undetected failures.
worksheet.consequence: Protection degrades from SIL-3 (PFD 1e-4) to a single transmitter (order 1e-3), so the 35% relief credit cannot be claimed and PSV-101/flare becomes the only pressure barrier.
worksheet.safeguard: 1oo2 PT with DC 0.6, diagnostics and partial-stroke test; PSV-101 as independent relief; bypass permit.
worksheet.action: Provide independent impulse lines and root valves per transmitter, a PT-out-of-service alarm with compensating action, and prohibit single-PT operation in the SIL-3 bypass procedure (HAZ-02, HAZ-03).

worksheet.deviation: HIPPS bypassed or proof-tested with the HP inlet live
worksheet.cause: The 12-month proof test and partial stroke are performed on a live train under a bypass permit; bypass left in place after the test or a nuisance trip; no independent high-pressure trip.
worksheet.consequence: Zero SIL-3 protection above the 66 barg PSV set; a well surge then relies on PSV-101 and a flare at 91.1% (107.5% at +18%); a left-in bypass converts every overpressure into a no-credit PSV-only event.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: HIPPS proof test and bypass restricted to shutdown, with a rate cap, independent approval and key-lock; PSV-101.
worksheet.action: Issue the SIL-3 bypass/proof-test procedure with time limit, key-lock, BPCS bypass alarm, compensating measures and a rate cap that keeps the no-credit case inside flare capacity; add the bypass case to the relief study (HAZ-03).

worksheet.deviation: HP interface level high: water into the oil outlet
worksheet.cause: LCV-102 stuck or plugged by scale or sand in the 8 in draw-off, interface transmitter fouled by emulsion/wax, and water cut rising toward 57% with the weir unchanged.
worksheet.consequence: Water is carried under with the oil into two-phase V-102/V-103, which have no water draw-off; condensate export goes off-spec (BS&W) and, at the extreme, water covers the gas outlet and carries over to K-101.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: independent 1oo2 LAHH/LSHH on V-101 tied to ESD, interface-specific measurement, boot/weir; LIC-102/LCV-102 modulating loop.
worksheet.action: Complete the 1oo2 LAHH/LSHH cause-and-effect and interface measurement, add a boot/weir and a water-cut sampling/response procedure, and confirm the coalescer carries the 17.09 s interface duty (HAZ-06).

worksheet.deviation: HP interface level low: water carried under with the oil
worksheet.cause: LCV-102 fails open or is driven open by a faulty level signal; LIC-101 drains the interface; draw-off exceeds the 2,782 bbl/d inflow during a rate change.
worksheet.consequence: Water enters V-102 at 10 bara, flashes and accumulates with no boot, then reaches K-102A or the stock tank; water to compression with no suction scrubber risks impeller erosion and seal damage.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: LCV-102 fail-closed, independent LSHH on V-101 to ESD, LIC-102 interface loop.
worksheet.action: Verify LCV-102 fail-closed action on air/power loss, add a low-interface ESD response and a water-draw-off rate limit, and confirm MP/LP water handling (HAZ-06, HAZ-12).

worksheet.deviation: HP gas rate above separator capacity (99.8% at K 0.11; 118.9% at 163.4 MMscfd)
worksheet.cause: Choke opened toward the 163.4 MMscfd well potential before the internals change; vendor K 0.14 not achieved (cap near 137.4 MMscfd); higher gas/oil ratio than the year-ten forecast.
worksheet.consequence: Vane-pack flooding and liquid carryover to K-101 with only 0.3 MMscfd margin at the base case; after the internals change the cap is 174.9 MMscfd, leaving 93.4% at well potential and little margin.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B internals: inlet device, vane pack, K 0.14 m/s (vendor expectation); mist eliminator; HIPPS and choke rate control.
worksheet.action: Obtain a vendor performance guarantee for K 0.14 m/s with a carryover test, add a gas-velocity/rate alarm and a cap at 93% of the guaranteed capacity, and verify the 163.4 MMscfd case (HAZ-06, HAZ-15).

worksheet.deviation: Liquid (oil/water) carryover in the HP gas to K-101
worksheet.cause: Gas rate at or above the K factor, damaged or fouled mist eliminator, foaming/emulsion at 48.7% cut and rising, or high oil level covering the gas outlet; there is no K-101 suction knock-out drum.
worksheet.consequence: Liquid reaches the K-101 impellers and dry-gas seals (no suction scrubber): erosion, rotor imbalance, seal failure with gas-fire potential, and trip of the 1,869 mol/s export stream.
worksheet.safeguard: V-101 vane pack/mist eliminator; Rev B 1oo2 LAHH to ESD; HIPPS; compressor dry-gas-seal system.
worksheet.action: Add a K-101 suction knock-out drum/coalescer or justify carryover tolerance with the vendor, install a liquid-detection trip, and set a foam/emulsion response procedure (HAZ-08).

worksheet.deviation: Loss of LIC-102 or instrument air, with LCV-102 failing open and gas blowing by to the 25 barg water package
worksheet.cause: Instrument-air loss with a fail-open or undefined LCV-102 fail position; seat/trim erosion after ten years passing gas at normal level; transmitter failure driving the valve fully open.
worksheet.consequence: 60 bara gas into V-105/V-106 (25 barg design) and the 8 in ANSI 300 water line; coalescer or hydrocyclone rupture with hydrocarbon release to the water deck.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: LCV-102 fail-closed, package high-pressure trip and PSV-104 on V-106 sized for gas blowby, independent LSHH/LAHH to ESD; 25 barg package design.
worksheet.action: Confirm the PSV-104 blowby sizing and the 25 barg ratings of V-105/V-106, add a high-pressure trip on the water package and a package ESD, and verify fail-closed action on air failure (HAZ-06, HAZ-14).

worksheet.deviation: V-102 overpressure above its 10 bara duty
worksheet.cause: VLV-102 fails open, passing 60 bara HP liquid and gas into V-102; K-102A trip or MP gas outlet blockage with the let-down still open; level control failure or carryover blocking the gas outlet.
worksheet.consequence: V-102 (existing, 3 mm CA) is taken above its 10 bara design; gas blowby to V-103 and the stock tank, or loss of containment at the MP vessel.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: PSV-102 on V-102 and PSV-103 on V-103, both sized for gas blowby; VLV-102/LV-101 let-down control.
worksheet.action: Confirm the V-102 design pressure and PSV-102 blowby sizing, add an independent high-pressure trip/ESDV on the MP let-down, and proof-test VLV-102 (HAZ-12, HAZ-14).

worksheet.deviation: V-102 liquid level high with carryover to K-102A
worksheet.cause: VLV-102 overfeeds after a level or flow upset; VLV-103 restricted or V-103 backed up; water carry-under from the HP stage raises the apparent level.
worksheet.consequence: Liquid into K-102A, which has no suction scrubber: erosion, imbalance and seal damage on one of the three MP trains; MP gas to the sales mixer falls and the K-101 flow split changes.
worksheet.safeguard: V-102 level control (BPCS); compressor high-level trip not identified; K-102A antisurge.
worksheet.action: Add an independent high-level trip and a suction knock-out drum on K-102A, and re-tune V-102 level control for the re-rated flow split (HAZ-08, HAZ-12).

worksheet.deviation: Water carried into the two-phase MP and LP stages, which have no water draw-off
worksheet.cause: HP interface low or an emulsion passing water with the oil; V-102 and V-103 are two-phase by design with no boot; an upset in the HP water draw-off.
worksheet.consequence: Water accumulates in V-102/V-103 and is carried to K-102A/K-103A or the stock tank; condensate off-spec and water in the 6 in export line; corrosion of carbon-steel MP/LP vessels where the 3 mm CA assumes water leaves at V-101.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B LSHH/LAHH on V-101 and LCV-102 fail-closed; V-102/V-103 3 mm CA with continuous CO2 inhibition.
worksheet.action: Provide water draw-off or a water-detection trip on V-102/V-103, review CO2 inhibition and CA for wet MP/LP service, and extend the water-cut procedure to the MP/LP stages (HAZ-12).

worksheet.deviation: Cold start after the four-week shutdown with hydrate or ice in VLV-102 and V-102
worksheet.cause: Wet gas (13.45 mol% water) at 10 bara entering a vessel at -5 C ambient; no hydrate inhibitor and flow assurance explicitly excluded from the basis; restart before V-102 is warmed through.
worksheet.consequence: Hydrate or ice plug in the let-down or MP gas line with overpressure upstream at VLV-102; delayed first gas and a second depressurisation of the MP stage.
worksheet.safeguard: Startup sequence and operating procedure; no hydrate inhibitor; V-102 not insulated or traced.
worksheet.action: Add hydrate prediction and methanol/glycol injection or warm-up for the cold-start case, and protect VLV-102/V-102 against a plugged outlet (HAZ-12).

worksheet.node: 4. LP let-down and stock tank: VLV-103, V-103, E-104, V-104
worksheet.deviation: Stock-tank flash gas over-pressures the fuel-gas system or back-pressures V-104
worksheet.cause: Flash gas from the 1.013 bara stock tank is routed to the fuel-gas header without a defined let-down/compression control; the flash line can block or be undersized and fuel-gas header pressure can exceed the tank rating.
worksheet.consequence: V-104 back-pressured above its 1.013 bara rating, or the fuel-gas system contaminated and over-pressured; loss of vapour recovery and a vent path on the stock tank.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: stock-tank flash gas corrected to the fuel-gas system (no longer routed to the 90 bara sales header); V-104 vent; fuel-gas pressure control.
worksheet.action: Confirm the flash-gas let-down/compression and fuel-gas header pressure control, and verify V-104 cannot be back-pressured above its rating (HAZ-14).

worksheet.node: 4. LP let-down and stock tank: VLV-103, V-103, E-104, V-104
worksheet.deviation: LP let-down overpressure: VLV-103 fails open into 2 bara V-103 and the 1.013 bara stock tank
worksheet.cause: VLV-103 fails open, passing 10 bara MP liquid and gas into V-103; P-101 trip or condensate-export backpressure; no independent high-pressure trip or relief was identified for V-103/V-104.
worksheet.consequence: V-103 (2 bara) and V-104 (1.013 bara) are overpressured, with gas blowby to the stock tank and a condensate release/fire at the tank; the relief case was not in the original basis.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: PSV-103 on V-103 sized for gas blowby; V-104 vent; VLV-103 let-down control.
worksheet.action: Confirm V-103/V-104 design pressures and PSV-103 blowby sizing, add an independent high-pressure trip/ESDV on the LP let-down, and proof-test VLV-103 (HAZ-12, HAZ-14).

worksheet.node: 4. LP let-down and stock tank: VLV-103, V-103, E-104, V-104
worksheet.deviation: V-104 stock tank overfill or LP liquid carryover
worksheet.cause: P-101 trip or condensate-line backpressure stops export; V-103 level high carries liquid through E-104; E-104 flooding or a blocked condensate flash line.
worksheet.consequence: 2,936 bbl/d of condensate overflows to the deck or drain with fire and pollution risk; liquid carryover to the flash-gas route and the sales header.
worksheet.safeguard: V-103 level control with PSV-103 on V-103, P-101 condensate pump (42 kW driver), V-104 vent.
worksheet.action: Add independent high-level trips on V-103/V-104, P-101 minimum-flow/auto-restart and a bunded closed-drain route, and verify E-104 flooding (HAZ-12).

worksheet.node: 4. LP let-down and stock tank: VLV-103, V-103, E-104, V-104
worksheet.deviation: E-104 outlet below 288 K with wax or ice in V-104 and the 6 in condensate line
worksheet.cause: Cooler over-performance at -5 C ambient or a colder letdown; wet condensate freezing in the stock tank; wax cloud point above 288 K for the gassier year-ten condensate.
worksheet.consequence: Wax or ice plugs the 15 km, 25 bara condensate line and loses condensate export; overpressure upstream of the plug between P-101 and the blockage.
worksheet.safeguard: E-104 cooler; 288 K operating basis; no insulation or tracing identified.
worksheet.action: Add outlet temperature control, insulation or tracing on E-104 and the condensate line, verify the wax cloud point, and add a blocked-line overpressure trip/PSV (HAZ-12).

worksheet.node: 4. LP let-down and stock tank: VLV-103, V-103, E-104, V-104
worksheet.deviation: Free water in the stock tank and the condensate export
worksheet.cause: Water carry-under from V-101 through the two-phase MP/LP stages; no water draw-off on V-104 and E-104 condenses water at 288 K; an emulsion not broken by the HP internals change.
worksheet.consequence: Condensate off-spec (BS&W) at the 2,936-3,466 bbl/d export rate; wet CO2 corrosion of the 6 in X65 line with 3 mm CA; reception penalties.
worksheet.safeguard: V-101 internals and LCV-102 fail-closed; 3 mm CA and CO2 inhibition; BS&W monitoring.
worksheet.action: Add condensate dehydration/draw-off or a BS&W analyser with automatic diversion, and review corrosion inhibition for the 6 in line (HAZ-12, HAZ-13).

worksheet.node: 5. Compression: K-101, K-102 A/B/C, K-103 A-E
worksheet.deviation: Compressor surge at low flow, including after the re-rate
worksheet.cause: Turndown to 60% with new impellers moving the surge line and the recycle not re-tuned; K-101 trip while K-102/K-103 discharge into the 90 bara mixer; a blocked export raises discharge pressure.
worksheet.consequence: Surge cycles damage thrust bearings and dry-gas seals; seal failure releases HP gas; export train trip with loss of 137.1-161.8 MMscfd and a V-101 overpressure/flare event.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: anti-surge recycle with cooler and revised curve; independent overspeed trip; compressor high-pressure trip.
worksheet.action: Issue the revised surge curve and anti-surge/recycle-cooler sizing, perform the surge/performance test and re-tune the recycle for 60% turndown (HAZ-08).

worksheet.node: 5. Compression: K-101, K-102 A/B/C, K-103 A-E
worksheet.deviation: K-101 power above the driver (2,689 kW against 2,300 kW, 116.9%)
worksheet.cause: Well potential of 163.4 MMscfd reached before the driver re-rate; fouled coolers or 35 C ambient; higher molecular weight or a changed flow split; the basis says one stage while the datasheet/P&ID show two.
worksheet.consequence: Driver overload trip or motor damage, losing the export train and triggering a V-101 overpressure event; the 22-week driver is long-lead, so the facility can run at 163.4 MMscfd on the old driver.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: driver confirmed at 2.7 MW with revised curve; existing 2,300 kW driver; compressor high-pressure trip.
worksheet.action: Complete the 2.7 MW driver re-rate and confirm stage count, impeller stress and absorbed power at 35 C/163.4 MMscfd before operating above 137.1 MMscfd (HAZ-09).

worksheet.node: 5. Compression: K-101, K-102 A/B/C, K-103 A-E
worksheet.deviation: K-101 suction below 60 bara
worksheet.cause: V-101 pressure low on turndown or after a HIPPS/SDV closure; K-101 surge or a restricted gas outlet; high HP liquid level reducing the gas space.
worksheet.consequence: Compression ratio, discharge temperature and power rise and the driver trips; V-101 liquid flashes, feeding two-phase flow to the compressor.
worksheet.safeguard: K-101 high-ratio trip/antisurge; V-101 pressure control by choke; HIPPS.
worksheet.action: Add a low-suction-pressure trip/recycle to the compressor protection and verify the high-ratio envelope with the re-rated impellers (HAZ-08, HAZ-09).

worksheet.node: 5. Compression: K-101, K-102 A/B/C, K-103 A-E
worksheet.deviation: Reverse flow from the 90 bara sales mixer into a tripped K-102 or K-103 train
worksheet.cause: Discharge check-valve failure on a tripped train; startup with the sales header already at 90 bara; K-102C or K-103E trip while the other trains hold the header.
worksheet.consequence: 90 bara gas into intercoolers and casings rated for 4-43 bara stage pressure; rupture of a low-pressure intercooler or casing with gas release and fire.
worksheet.safeguard: Discharge check valves; compressor high-pressure trip; train ESD (no discharge ESDV identified).
worksheet.action: Verify/upgrade discharge check valves and add an ESDV/SSIV on each train discharge or the 90 bara header with a reverse-flow interlock (HAZ-10, HAZ-13).

worksheet.node: 5. Compression: K-101, K-102 A/B/C, K-103 A-E
worksheet.deviation: Liquid or water into K-101, K-102A or K-103A
worksheet.cause: Separator carryover from nodes 2 and 3; there are no suction knock-out drums on any train; higher mist carryover at the K 0.14 gas velocity; water from the two-phase MP/LP stages.
worksheet.consequence: Impeller erosion, imbalance, dry-gas-seal damage and a potential gas fire; intercooler fouling and an unplanned train outage.
worksheet.safeguard: Separator internals; dry-gas-seal system; Rev B high-level trips on V-101; no suction scrubbers.
worksheet.action: Provide suction knock-out drums/coalescers and liquid-detection trips on all three trains, and set a liquid-carryover operating limit (HAZ-08).

worksheet.node: 5. Compression: K-101, K-102 A/B/C, K-103 A-E
worksheet.deviation: Loss of power, instrument air or cooling to the three trains
worksheet.cause: Platform power failure or air-compressor trip; cooling-medium loss or 35 C ambient defeating the 313.15 K aftercooler approach; a common cause acting on the shared utilities.
worksheet.consequence: All trains trip; V-101 overpressure and 42.63 kg/s to the flare (91.1% now, 107.5% after the re-rate); loss of export and a black start with the flare as the only pressure sink.
worksheet.safeguard: Compressor trips and ESD, flare; no documented loss-of-utilities matrix (Rev B F&G/ESD philosophy added).
worksheet.action: Produce the loss-of-utilities matrix (power, air, cooling, seal gas) with ride-through/trip philosophy, verify the 4,630 kW aftercooler duty at 35 C, and add the total-trip case to the relief study (HAZ-09, HAZ-01).

worksheet.node: 6. Produced-water package: V-105 hydrocyclone, V-106 coalescer, P-102
worksheet.deviation: No flow through the produced-water package (P-102 trip or blockage)
worksheet.cause: Single P-102 with no installed spare; hydrocyclone liner or coalescer plugging by solids/scale; reject-valve failure; the datasheet 18.4 m3/h is the current duty, not the 39.7 m3/h required.
worksheet.consequence: Water backs up to V-101 with only about 8 min retention at 2,782 bbl/d before the interface reaches the oil/gas outlet; oil to the gas outlet/compressor or water to condensate; rate cut or trip.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: P-102 2 x 50% at 40 m3/h, V-106 coalescer 4.0 m T/T (6.5 min), OIW analyser; existing 3,000 bbl/d plant.
worksheet.action: Confirm the 2 x 50% P-102 installation and auto-start/standby changeover, and add a low-flow/water-backup trip to ESD (HAZ-07).

worksheet.node: 6. Produced-water package: V-105 hydrocyclone, V-106 coalescer, P-102
worksheet.deviation: Water rate above package capacity, or one 50% hydrocyclone liner blocked
worksheet.cause: Water cut rising to 57% (~3,250 bbl/d) with one 50% liner out; reject control valve failure or a surge from V-101; the old 3,000 bbl/d plant is already at 92.7%.
worksheet.consequence: Hydrocyclone/coalescer overload, oil-in-water above permit and water backup to V-101; before the upgrade the water plant caps gas at 147.8 MMscfd, stranding compressor and flare capacity.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B 2 x 50% V-105 hydrocyclone, V-106 6,000 bbl/d coalescer and OIW analyser; existing 3,000 bbl/d plant.
worksheet.action: Verify package performance at 57% cut, 60% turndown and one liner out, and set a water-rate cap with automatic diversion to slop (HAZ-07, HAZ-15).

worksheet.node: 6. Produced-water package: V-105 hydrocyclone, V-106 coalescer, P-102
worksheet.deviation: Produced water at 81 C against an 80 C package design
worksheet.cause: V-101 operates at 354.15 K (81 C) and there is no produced-water cooler; a hot well or reduced Joule-Thomson cooling raises the HP temperature.
worksheet.consequence: No design-temperature margin on V-105/V-106/P-102; 316L chloride pitting/SCC risk at 80 C and elastomer/gasket limits reached on a 25 barg package.
worksheet.safeguard: 316L/Super Duplex materials; 80 C package design; V-101 at 81 C.
worksheet.action: Add a produced-water cooler or raise the package design temperature, review 316L chloride SCC and elastomer limits at 81 C, and add a high-temperature alarm (HAZ-07, HAZ-14).

worksheet.node: 6. Produced-water package: V-105 hydrocyclone, V-106 coalescer, P-102
worksheet.deviation: Oil carryover to overboard or reinjection water
worksheet.cause: Interface settling is 17.09 s against a 60 s class check, so the coalescer is the only barrier; coalescer bypass/media damage or an emulsion; solids loading the coalescer.
worksheet.consequence: Oil-in-water permit exceedance on 2,782 bbl/d of produced water; reinjection-well fouling and loss of disposal capacity.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: OIW analyser with automatic diversion to slop and overboard valve interlock; V-106 coalescer (6.5 min).
worksheet.action: Set the OIW permit limit and diversion logic, add a coalescer differential-pressure/bypass alarm, and confirm the analyser maintenance and calibration plan (HAZ-07).

worksheet.node: 6. Produced-water package: V-105 hydrocyclone, V-106 coalescer, P-102
worksheet.deviation: Reverse flow from the disposal or reinjection header into the 25 barg package
worksheet.cause: Disposal well shut in or reinjection header above 25 barg; P-102 discharge check-valve failure; historically no PSV on V-105/V-106.
worksheet.consequence: V-106 coalescer (25 barg design) overpressured from downstream with coalescer rupture and produced-water/hydrocarbon release; in the extreme backflow to V-101 through a failed LCV-102.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: PSV-104 on V-106, P-102 discharge check valve; 8 in 316L ANSI 300 line; LCV-102 fail-closed.
worksheet.action: Confirm PSV-104 reverse-case sizing and non-return protection at the disposal battery limit, and add a high-pressure trip on the package (HAZ-06, HAZ-14).

worksheet.deviation: Loss of relief path: flare or header out of service, or PSV-101 inlet blocked
worksheet.cause: Flare tip/header replacement or isolation with wells online; pilot/purge loss or header liquid blockage; PSV inlet block valve left closed/car-sealed, or iron-carbonate/hydrate plugging in the 4 in inlet.
worksheet.consequence: PSV-101 has no disposal route or fails to lift; V-101 exceeds 66 barg toward 72.6 bara MIP with loss of containment; the HIPPS becomes the only barrier and is not a relief device.
worksheet.safeguard: PSV-101 6.38 in2 at 66 barg; flare pilots/purge; HIPPS SIL-3; PSV re-certification.
worksheet.action: Add a flare-outage/PSV-impairment procedure with a rate cap and HP shutdown trigger, car-seal/lock the PSV inlet valve open, and add flare pilot/purge and header-liquid alarms (HAZ-04, HAZ-05).

worksheet.deviation: PSV outlet or header back pressure derates the conventional PSV
worksheet.cause: The 6 in outlet must carry 42.63 kg/s (~40 m3/s) at 1.5 barg, far above a 6 in tailpipe; the flare runs at 91.1%/107.5%; a restricted tailpipe or superimposed back pressure above the 1.5 bar assumption.
worksheet.consequence: A conventional PSV loses capacity as back pressure rises (chattering, reduced lift, V-101 overpressure); the 6.38 in2 orifice passes the mass but the outlet, not the orifice, becomes the constraint.
worksheet.safeguard: PSV-101 conventional P orifice, 4 in inlet x 6 in outlet; 1.5 bar back-pressure assumption; existing flare.
worksheet.action: Perform the API 520 inlet/outlet hydraulic study at 42.63 and 50.31 kg/s, fit a balanced-bellows PSV or enlarge the outlet, and verify the 3% inlet/10% back-pressure limits (HAZ-04).

worksheet.deviation: PSV set pressure equals the vessel design (66 barg), with maximum incidental pressure at 72.6 bara
worksheet.cause: PSV set at design pressure with no margin for set-point drift; the blocked-outlet case takes V-101 to 72.6 bara (110% of design); back pressure or slow opening adds accumulation.
worksheet.consequence: Any set-point error or back pressure puts the 66 barg shell above design; relief at 110% is the code maximum and leaves no margin on a ten-year-old shell with 3 mm CA; nozzle/flange leakage and fatigue.
worksheet.safeguard: PSV-101 set 66 barg with 72.6 bara accumulation limit; PSV re-certification; 66 barg vessel design.
worksheet.action: Review the PSV set pressure against the 72.6 bara MIP and vessel CA, add set-point verification and a spare PSV, and confirm the relief/re-rate basis under MOC (HAZ-04, HAZ-14).

worksheet.deviation: Relief above the credited 32.70 kg/s when the HIPPS fails to close at the re-rated rate
worksheet.cause: SDV-101 fails to close, or the HIPPS is bypassed or its proof test overdue; the 35% credit is 0.65 x 50.31 kg/s and only 23.3% below the current 42.63 kg/s case; well potential pushes the case to 50.3 kg/s.
worksheet.consequence: 50.3 kg/s is 107.5% of the 46.34 kg/s flare; radiation grows to 82.4 m against 75.0 m now and 64.0 m with the credit, beyond the unverified sterile area; flameout and liquid carryover.
worksheet.safeguard: HIPPS 35% credit (conditional), PSV-101 and the 46.34 kg/s flare; +25% flare fallback identified but not selected.
worksheet.action: Prove the 35% credit by dynamic relief study or book the 50.31 kg/s no-credit case and select the +25% flare/header fallback or a rate cap; re-issue the PSV, flare and radiation basis under MOC (HAZ-01).

worksheet.deviation: Simultaneous relief from HP plus MP, LP or fire exceeds 46.34 kg/s
worksheet.cause: Shared flare header with the HP blocked outlet coincident with a K-102/K-103 trip or an MP/LP PSV lift; a fire in another area adds its relief load; no load-shedding or sequential-blowdown philosophy.
worksheet.consequence: The flare goes above 100% with the HP case alone at 91.1%; header back pressure rises and PSVs stall; the radiation contour expands beyond 82.4 m with possible flameout.
worksheet.safeguard: Flare header 46.34 kg/s; PSV-101 plus PSV-102/103/104; no sequential blowdown or load shedding.
worksheet.action: Add a relief load summary and a sequential-blowdown/load-shedding philosophy, and include the coincident HP+MP/LP+fire case in the flare hydraulic study (HAZ-01, HAZ-04).

worksheet.deviation: SIMOPS: flare-header hot work or tie-in during the four-week shutdown with HP live on another front
worksheet.cause: Four parallel work fronts with header/tip work while wells and HP separation stay online; isolation by a single blind or valve; the water-package tie-in at V-101 is also live; hot-work permit over a hydrocarbon-bearing system.
worksheet.consequence: Ignition of a hydrocarbon release with the flare path removed; injury or fatality potential and loss of the relief path for the live HP train.
worksheet.safeguard: Shutdown plan, permit-to-work and isolation philosophy; the risk register rates SIMOPS likelihood low; no SIMOPS matrix.
worksheet.action: Produce the SIMOPS matrix/risk assessment, impairment register, flare-outage and emergency response plan, and re-baseline the schedule and commissioning duration before sanction (HAZ-11).

worksheet.deviation: Fire on the HP train with the flare out or PSV-101 isolated, with no depressurisation
worksheet.cause: The 0.54 kg/s fire case relies on PIR insulation and drainage not specified as fire-rated; there is no BDV/blowdown on V-101 or the HP inlet spool; PSV-101 can be isolated for maintenance.
worksheet.consequence: No relief path and no depressurisation for the 66 barg inventory; V-101 and its nozzles heat up, and with PSV-101 isolated the HIPPS is the only barrier; escalation to rupture and jet fire.
worksheet.safeguard: Rev B: F&G/ESD philosophy and BDV scope added to FEED; PSV-101; PIR 50 mm insulation (not fire-rated).
worksheet.action: Add BDV/blowdown on V-101 and the HP inlet spool with F&G-to-ESD cause and effect, specify fire-rated insulation/fireproofing, and assess the fire case with PSV-101 isolated (HAZ-10, HAZ-05).

worksheet.deviation: Reverse flow from the 25 bara condensate line into the 1.013 bara stock tank
worksheet.cause: P-101 trip or check-valve failure on the 6 in export line; reception pressure above 25 bara or the line shut in at reception; no non-return protection at the battery limit.
worksheet.consequence: Near-atmospheric V-104 overpressured by up to 25 bara with tank rupture and a 2,936 bbl/d condensate release and fire; reverse flow also carries water and wax back into the tank.
worksheet.safeguard: P-101 condensate pump and discharge check valve; V-104 vent; 25 bara condensate line.
worksheet.action: Add a non-return valve/ESDV at the condensate battery limit and a V-104 high-pressure trip/vent, and verify the 25 bara reverse case in the line relief study (HAZ-13).

worksheet.deviation: Reception or export-line pressure above 90 bara
worksheet.cause: Downstream reception shut in or compression raising line pressure; blockage/hydrate with thermal expansion of a blocked-in 15 km line; reverse flow into the 90 bara platform system (100 barg design).
worksheet.consequence: K-101 driven toward surge or stonewall with the sales mixer and discharge above 90 bara; overpressure of the 12 in X65 line (100 barg design) or reverse flow through the compressor.
worksheet.safeguard: 12 in X65, 100 barg design; compressor high-pressure trip; no ESDV/SSIV or line relief at the battery limit.
worksheet.action: Add an ESDV/SSIV and an independent high-pressure trip/line relief at the export battery limit, and verify the blocked-in thermal expansion case (HAZ-13).

worksheet.deviation: Water-saturated export gas: hydrate and corrosion in the 15 km line
worksheet.cause: Dehydration is assumed from an existing TEG unit but its capacity at 161.8 MMscfd and 3 lb/MMscf is unverified; the 313.15 K aftercooler leaves the gas saturated upstream (~15 kg/MMscf) with no hydrate/corrosion inhibitor downstream; CO2 at 1.22 mol% and seabed cooldown below 10 C at 60 bara.
worksheet.consequence: Hydrate plug at 60 bara and low temperature with loss of export and pressure build-up at the platform; wet CO2 corrosion of X65 with 3 mm CA over 15 km, and slugging/water dropout at reception.
worksheet.safeguard: Existing TEG dehydration (assumed, capacity unverified); aftercooler at 313.15 K; 3LPP coating and 3 mm CA; no hydrate/corrosion inhibitor downstream.
worksheet.action: Verify the existing TEG dehydration capacity at 161.8 MMscfd to 3 lb/MMscf, add hydrate/corrosion inhibition and a water-dew-point alarm, and include the 15 km line in the two-barrier (NORSOK S-001) and integrity assessment (HAZ-16, HAZ-13).

worksheet.deviation: Partial blockage (hydrate, wax, pig or debris) in the 12 in gas or 6 in condensate line
worksheet.cause: Hydrate or wax deposition, a stuck pig, 3LPP/debris in the line, or a restricted reception valve.
worksheet.consequence: Backpressure rises, K-101 approaches surge and the rate falls below 161.8 MMscfd; overpressure between the blockage and the platform, and pig or line damage.
worksheet.safeguard: Compressor high-pressure trip; pigging (no procedure); line design margin.
worksheet.action: Write the pigging and blockage-response procedure with platform rate/pressure triggers, and add a line-pressure alarm and surge-protection review (HAZ-13).

worksheet.deviation: Pipeline blowdown or pigging to the platform flare exceeds 46.34 kg/s
worksheet.cause: The 12 in x 15 km line at 60-90 bara holds of order 55 t of gas and its blowdown is routed to the flare; pigging, depressurisation or emergency venting with no restriction or staged blowdown.
worksheet.consequence: Initial blowdown rate far above the 46.34 kg/s flare design with flare overload and radiation beyond 82.4 m; liquid carryover to the flare and possible flameout.
worksheet.safeguard: Flare 46.34 kg/s; no staged-blowdown restriction or dedicated vent.
worksheet.action: Add a restricted/staged blowdown and pigging procedure with a calculated rate limit, and verify the pipeline blowdown case against the flare and radiation contours (HAZ-01, HAZ-13).

actions.finding: The 35% HIPPS relief credit (50.31 to 32.70 kg/s) is a study assumption with no dynamic relief study or device-specific SIL verification; it is the sole basis for preferring the HIPPS scope over the +25% flare/header fallback.
actions.action: Commission the dynamic relief study (HIPPS <2 s closure, trapped inventory, SDV leakage, PSV/flare response) plus device-specific SIL verification before booking the credit. If 35% is not proven, book 50.31 kg/s, select the +25% flare/header fallback or a rate cap, and re-issue the PSV, flare and radiation basis under MOC.

actions.finding: HIPPS PFD 1e-4/SIL 3 is asserted from a partially verified library determination; the P&ID shows both PTs upstream of SDV-101, the final element is a single SDV, and no trip setpoint or response time is defined.
actions.action: Perform IEC 61508/61511 SIL verification with device failure rates, CCF beta, proof-test effectiveness, partial-stroke coverage and final-element PFD; confirm PT taps are downstream of SDV-101; define setpoint, deadband and response time; re-derive the SIL target from a LOPA (the PSV already passes the +18% case at 86.7%).

actions.finding: Any full-rate HIPPS bypass or in-service proof test puts the plant on the no-credit relief case (50.31 kg/s, 107.5% of flare) and outside the design basis.
actions.action: Issue the SIL-3 bypass/proof-test procedure with independent approval, time limit, key-lock, BPCS bypass alarm, compensating measures and a rate cap or curtailment that keeps the no-credit case inside flare capacity; prohibit bypass during the four-week SIMOPS campaign and add the bypass case to the relief study.

actions.finding: PSV-101 inlet pressure drop and built-up back pressure are not calculated; the conventional PSV assumes 1.5 bar constant back pressure while the flare runs at 91-107.5% of capacity.
actions.action: Perform the API 520 inlet/outlet hydraulic study at 42.63 and 50.31 kg/s: verify inlet dP at or below 3% of set and built-up back pressure at or below 10% (or fit balanced bellows), confirm the 66 barg set and 72.6 bara accumulation, and provide a spare PSV or an isolation/impairment procedure.

actions.finding: The 4.73 kW/m2 radiation contour is 64.0 m with HIPPS and 82.4 m without, but the sterile area, escape routes and temporary refuge are not verified and only one contour is reported.
actions.action: Verify the 64.0 m and 82.4 m contours against the platform sterile area, escape routes and temporary refuge; add the 1.58 kW/m2 personnel and 6.3 kW/m2 equipment contours; confirm flare tip exit velocity, ignition, purge and knock-out drum; select the fallback if the 82.4 m contour is not clear.

actions.finding: V-101 had single-loop level/interface control with no independent LAHH/LSHH, 17.09 s settling against a 60 s criterion, and an LCV-102 fail-open path admitting 60 bara gas into the 25 barg water package.
actions.action: Implement independent 1oo2 LAHH/LSHH on V-101 tied to ESD, interface-specific measurement, a boot/weir and LCV-102 fail-closed; confirm the coalescer carries the 17.09 s interface duty and that PSV-104 protects V-106 against gas blowby.

actions.finding: The produced-water package could not deliver 6,000 bbl/d as datasheeted: P-102 18.4 m3/h against 39.7 m3/h and V-106 3.76 min against a 6.5 min claim, with no standby, OIW analyser or diversion.
actions.action: Re-scope to P-102 2 x 50% at 40 m3/h and the V-106 coalescer at 4.0 m T/T (6.5 min), add the OIW analyser with automatic diversion to slop and an overboard valve interlock, and write the package bypass/permit procedure.

actions.finding: The K-101 re-rate left 2,689 kW against a 2,300 kW driver (116.9%) with no surge, overspeed or recycle case, and the 1-stage/2-stage description is inconsistent.
actions.action: Confirm the driver at 2.7 MW, issue the revised compressor curve with anti-surge valve and recycle-cooler sizing, add an independent overspeed trip and API 617 test, and update the operating procedures and alarm/trip setpoints.

actions.finding: The re-rated train has no torsional/lateral, impeller-stress or loss-of-utilities case, and the aftercooler duty rises to 4,630 kW with a single TIC-101 loop.
actions.action: Perform torsional/lateral and impeller-stress analysis, define the dry-gas-seal and loss-of-utilities (power, air, cooling, seal gas) response, confirm the 4,630 kW aftercooler duty at 35 C, resolve the 1 vs 2 stage discrepancy, and obtain the vendor performance guarantee at 35 C/163.4 MMscfd.

actions.finding: No F&G philosophy, ESD hierarchy, depressurisation/blowdown, fireproofing or temporary-refuge/escape-route assessment was documented for a manned platform.
actions.action: Produce the F&G and ESD cause and effect (ESD-1/2/3), add BDV/blowdown on V-101 and the HP inlet spool, ESDV/SSIV on the export gas and condensate lines, F&G coverage for the HP inlet, compressor and water package, fireproofing for structural steel/SDV/PSV/flare header, and a temporary-refuge and escape-route assessment.

actions.finding: The four-week shutdown puts four parallel work fronts on a live hydrocarbon platform with 0.8 week commissioning, no SIMOPS matrix, and a SIMOPS risk rated Low.
actions.action: Produce the SIMOPS matrix and risk assessment (hot work, isolation, gas-freeing, dropped objects, flare outage, marine movements), an impairment register for PSV/ESD/HIPPS/F&G, a flare-outage and emergency response plan, and re-baseline the schedule and commissioning duration before sanction.

actions.finding: Let-down overpressure was unprotected: VLV-102 failure puts 60 bara into 10 bara V-102, and VLV-103 puts 10 bara into 2 bara V-103 and the 1.013 bara V-104, with no design pressures or PSVs stated.
actions.action: Bring PSV-102 on V-102 and PSV-103 on V-103 into scope (protection credited, sizing calculation to detailed design), confirm V-102/V-103/V-104 design pressures and relief cases, add independent high-pressure trips/ESDVs on the let-down valves, and proof-test VLV-102/103 with a blocked-outlet case.

actions.finding: The export gas and condensate lines have no ESDV/SSIV, no line relief, no two-barrier (NORSOK S-001) check and no verified dehydration capacity or hydrate/corrosion inhibition; the compressor trip is the only barrier.
actions.action: Extend the two-barrier assessment to the 100 barg export gas and 30 barg condensate lines, add ESDV/SSIV and independent high-pressure protection at the battery limit, specify the water dew point and hydrate/corrosion inhibition, and write the pigging, blockage and staged-blowdown procedures.

actions.finding: Relief sizing and PSV set-pressure margin are unresolved, and the relief valve register, inspection intervals and spare-PSV arrangement are not defined for the new duty.
actions.action: Complete the PSV-101/102/103/104 sizing and set-pressure review, issue the relief valve register with inspection intervals and the flare/PSV impairment matrix, and provide a spare PSV for PSV-101.

actions.finding: Key performance claims remain vendor expectations: V-101 internals K 0.14 m/s, V-106 6.5 min at 57% cut, P-102 40 m3/h and the re-rated compressor curve at 35 C have no guaranteed performance.
actions.action: Obtain binding vendor performance guarantees and witnessed tests for the V-101 internals (K 0.14 m/s with carryover), V-106 retention at 57% cut and 60% turndown, P-102 duty, and the compressor curve/power at 35 C and 163.4 MMscfd; carry the guarantees into the purchase orders.

actions.finding: The export gas relies on an assumed existing TEG dehydration unit whose capacity at 161.8 MMscfd to a 3 lb/MMscf specification is not verified, while the 313.15 K aftercooler leaves the gas saturated.
actions.action: Verify the existing TEG dehydration capacity at 161.8 MMscfd and a 3 lb/MMscf water specification (water dew point), confirm glycol regeneration/reboiler duty and turndown, and add a water-dew-point analyser with a high alarm; if capacity is short, add dehydration capacity or hydrate inhibition.

design_effect: Rev B adds independent 1oo2 LAHH/LSHH on V-101 tied to ESD, LCV-102 fail-closed and PSV-104 on V-106 coalescer, closing the 60 bara-to-25 barg gas-blowby path and removing reliance on the modulating LIC loops for level protection.

The produced-water package is re-scoped to P-102 2 x 50% at 40 m3/h and the V-106 coalescer at 4.0 m T/T (6.5 min) with an OIW analyser and diversion/interlock, so water no longer caps gas at about 147.8 MMscfd; performance at 57% cut remains a vendor-guarantee condition.

The compressor driver is confirmed at 2.7 MW with anti-surge recycle, a revised curve and an independent overspeed trip, closing the 116.9% overload; torsional, loss-of-utilities and API 617 cases remain detailed-design conditions.

HIPPS proof test and bypass are restricted to shutdown with a rate cap and independent approval; PSV-102 on V-102 and PSV-103 on V-103 are in scope, stock-tank flash gas is corrected to the fuel-gas system, and the F&G/ESD philosophy and BDV scope are added to the FEED package.

No finding invalidates the capacity conclusion of 161.8 MMscfd and about 3,466 bbl/d, but the 35% HIPPS credit (50.31 to 32.70 kg/s) remains conditional: without it the +18% case is 107.5% of the flare and the radiation contour is 82.4 m, so the +25% flare fallback or a rate cap applies.

Remaining conditions: dynamic relief, device-specific SIL verification, PSV inlet/back-pressure hydraulics and sterile-area verification stay open to the safety case; SIMOPS, compressor torsional/utility cases, vendor guarantees, relief sizing and the TEG dehydration capacity check stay open to detailed design.
